conclusion: On this 16GB Apple-silicon Mac, keeping 4B and 8B resident cost the 8B service about 0.37% mean throughput and about 1.0% p50 latency, but the tail was visibly worse: p95 rose from 250.7 ms alone to 301.0 ms when 4B was resident (+20.0% on the coexistence side). The extra resident 4B process accounted for about 5.6 GB of physical footprint. Recommendation: keep 4B resident if its independent capability is useful, because mean 8B throughput is nearly unchanged; stop 4B for latency-sensitive 8B tail workloads or when reclaiming roughly 5.6 GB is more valuable.

commands.stop_4b: kill -TERM 70733 70730  # 4B proxy then 4B server; both PIDs confirmed absent
